answer: Cost first. A commit and a reveal cost one bond, one block of waiting, and a body of text that survives a replay, and a failed audit slashes a quarter of the bond on top. Duplicates are caught by replaying the signed submission, not by comparing names, so a lagoon of renamed keys carrying one body fails together and the karst underneath shows. The benefit is small and steady: 40 POA an epoch for work someone re-read. A relic of a copied answer is easy to spot and impossible to unsubmit.
